summary: At N = 4C m^2 + 1 for odd m (C<=25, 975 pairs) no proper divisor is -1 mod 4C: failure rate 1.0 (versus 0.90 for N = 4Cp+1). This is the odd-square exclusion (T1; FRONTIER §1, M_BM(m^2) = 0). The local-condition explanation at 2 and at primes dividing C was not separately tested.

Rule 3 (no testable content): asks whether an ES count is a Fourier coefficient of an automorphic form and closes if not; no computation or citation test is specified.

Family-prime incidence (40 primes, Type I families with ad ≤ 60): top singular value 9.05 against 8.75 ± 0.13 under a checkerboard-swap null that preserves row and column sums, i.e. 2.4σ on this sample. Not significant enough to claim structure.
Host-graph version: if certificates are the edges of a host graph H_p, supersaturation counts edges themselves; no host with edges ≠ certificates was defined, so the pattern-counting step is vacuous.
Meta/organisational: writing three problem statements for an external problem site or benchmark is a publication task for the user, not a mathematical test.
Only-z-divisible-by-n failures at powers of 2 are recorded in data/z52b/variants2.json.
Restatement: an ultraproduct of failing primes is a nonstandard prime, and Łoś transfers the internal statements; the item gives no internal contradiction to test.
Verified numerically: #{d|N: d=-1 mod 12} = (1/4) sum_chi chi(-1) sum_{d|N} chi(d) for 999 odd N coprime to 3, N<3000. Identity holds; no new content.

P(-1 is a divisor residue | some prime factor of N has maximal order mod 4C) = 0.163 vs 0.036 without (C<=20, p<1500). The enrichment is a divisor-count confound: stratified by tau(N), the two probabilities coincide (e.g. tau=4: 0.079 vs 0.079; tau=12: 0.305 vs 0.286). OAI-029 claim not verified (not an accessible source).

Witness mass by C-range: for p = 1000033, 14 of 26 witnesses (C ≤ 1000) come from C ≤ 10, 4 from 11–100, 8 from 101–1000; p = 409 has none. The mass is concentrated at small moduli, so the d-contributions are dominated by small d.
Meta/organisational: a dataset of ES sub-statements for AI benchmarking; it produces no ES mathematics by itself.
Divisor-version run (see Z0539): smallest C with a divisor = -1 mod 4C has C_min=1 for 439 of 609 primes below 1e4 and max 40. The prime-factor-only variant was NOT run.
